videos.title: Toenail Fungus? Try This Before It Gets Worse!  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Toenail Fungus? Try This Before It Gets Worse!  Dr. Mandell Are your toenails turning yellow, becoming thick, brittle, discolored, or growing abnormally? You may be dealing with toenail fungus, also known as onychomycosis, a common fungal infection that can become increasingly difficult to manage over time. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the potential antifungal properties of oregano oil and its powerful natural compound called carvacrol, which has demonstrated the ability to interfere with fungal cell membranes in laboratory studies. Discover why fungus thrives in warm, dark, moist environments, how proper foot hygiene can help prevent reinfection, and why keeping your toenails trimmed, clean, and dry is so important. You'll also learn about emerging research involving essential oils and fungal nail infections. Although oregano oil shows promising antifungal activity, research has not established that oregano oil alone reliably cures toenail fungus, and concentrated essential oils can irritate the skin. Persistent or worsening nail changes should be evaluated by a healthcare professional because not every discolored nail is caused by fungus. Take care of your feet, protect your nails, and remember that healthy habits today can make a difference tomorrow! 
#toenailfungustreatment  #OreganoOil #NailFungus #HealthyFeet #DrAlanMandell #motivationaldoc 

PubMed Research
1. Essential Oils and Toenail Fungus — Clinical Study (2020)
Alessandrini A, et al. An Open Study to Evaluate Effectiveness and Tolerability of a Nail Oil Composed of Vitamin E and Essential Oils in Mild to Moderate Distal Subungual Onychomycosis.
Skin Appendage Disorders, 2020.
PMID: 32021856
A small clinical study of 20 patients evaluated a topical formulation containing oregano, tea tree, lime essential oils, and vitamin E, reporting promising results. This was a combination product, not oregano oil alone. 
2. Oregano Oil and Antifungal Activity — Laboratory Research (2024)
Scandorieiro S, et al. Nail Lacquer Containing Origanum vulgare and Rosmarinus officinalis Essential Oils and Biogenic Silver Nanoparticles for Onychomycosis: Development, Characterization, and Evaluation of Antifungal Efficacy.
Antibiotics, 2024.
PMID: 39335065

videos.title: Are Max & Red Bull Now The Team To Beat? | Singapore GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Are Max & Red Bull Now The Team To Beat? | Singapore GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast Max Verstappen secured back-to-back wins from pole position with his first ever victory at the Singapore Grand Prix. With seven podium finishes from the last eight races, at a range of different tracks, are he and Red Bull now the benchmark in Formula 1?

Tom Clarkson is joined in the paddock by Jolyon Palmer and James Hinchcliffe to discuss Max’s ‘masterclass’ around the Marina Bay Circuit and what we can expect from Red Bull for the rest of the season.

Charles Leclerc claimed his first podium in seven races with P2, but should he have taken the lead from Max at the start after a great launch at lights out? And if he had succeeded, could he have held on to win?

There was disappointment on the other side of the Ferrari garage, as Lewis Hamilton’s decision to stay out under the final Virtual Safety Car cost him a podium. He apologised to the team over the radio at the end of the race, but should they have been more forceful in asking him to pit?

The guys also discuss Kimi Antonelli’s ‘opportunistic’ drive to P3, the crash between McLaren teammates Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in the Sprint race and Liam Lawson’s future at Racing Bulls after another big points haul for the New Zealander.

01:15 – Red Bull the new benchmark?
12:59 – Mixed emotions at Ferrari
20:07 - ‘Opportunistic’ Kimi

41:49 – Awesome Lawson

Whether you want to lose body fat or build muscle, a healthy diet goes beyond counting calories. I'll explain my reasoning and what to look for when choosing foods.

First up: bananas. Are bananas bad for you? Do bananas make you fat? Bananas can fit into a balanced diet and a fat loss meal plan. The issue discussed here is what happens when you blend them into a smoothie alongside certain beneficial plant compounds.

A 2023 study investigated how polyphenol oxidase, an enzyme abundant in bananas, affects the availability of flavanols in smoothies. Under the conditions tested, the banana smoothie substantially reduced the measured availability of these compounds compared with the control. That is more specific than saying bananas destroy every antioxidant in your shake. If you're choosing smoothie ingredients to maximize flavanol intake, this research gives you something to consider. Eating a banana separately is a different question.

Next, we look at whole grain bread and comments from Dr. Robert Lustig about food processing. Terms such as "multigrain" and "made with whole grains" can make a loaf sound healthier without telling you how much whole grain it contains. Check the ingredient list, fiber content, added sugar and serving size instead of relying on the front of the package.

Grinding a grain into flour does not automatically stop it from being whole grain. However, the structure and processing of a food can influence how it is digested. The takeaway is to compare breads carefully and choose options that support your nutrition goals. Bread doesn't have to disappear from your diet to get lean.

Then comes white bean soup and a personal experience I won't forget. After eating it shortly before a severe gastrointestinal illness, I developed an aversion that still makes it difficult to enjoy. That explains my decision, but it doesn't make white beans a bad food. It also opens a discussion about soup labels.

With canned soup, pay attention to sodium and the number of servings per container. If the nutrition information is listed for one serving and you eat two, your actual intake is twice the listed amount. Compare options, look for lower-sodium varieties and consider what else you're eating that day. Convenience can fit into healthy eating, but knowing what is in the entire portion matters.

Artificial food dyes are another topic in this video, including Blue 1, Yellow 5, Yellow 6 and Red 40. Research has examined whether synthetic food colors can affect activity and attention in some children. That doesn't mean every dye causes ADHD or that every brightly colored food causes cancer. My preference is to question ingredients added mainly for appearance and choose alternatives when practical.

We also discuss farm-raised salmon and how feed influences its pink color. Pigments such as astaxanthin can be included in salmon feed, and they are different from the synthetic dyes discussed above. Watch for the reasoning behind my preference and a closer look at how food is produced.

You don't have to copy every food decision I make. Use this video to ask better questions about your diet, understand the difference between a personal aversion and a research finding, and eat better in 2026.

videos.title: OpenAI’s Secret AI Just Made Hundreds of New Discoveries In Mathematics
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s Secret AI Just Made Hundreds of New Discoveries In Mathematics https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI just published hundreds of AI-generated mathematics papers, claiming its unreleased GPT-6 variant has resolved more than 100 open problems. Some have challenged mathematicians for decades. Others touch the Riemann Hypothesis, Hilbert's Tenth Problem, and conjectures dating back to the 1960s.

But did OpenAI actually solve these problems? And how much of this mathematics has been independently verified?

On October 6, OpenAI released a GitHub repository containing more than 700 AI-generated manuscripts organized into 372 result families, reportedly produced by an internal model trained for roughly six weeks. The system tackled approximately 4,000 mathematical problems, with individual results averaging around three hours of compute.

The numbers are extraordinary. But the headlines leave out some critical distinctions.

A result family isn't necessarily a solved problem. A Lean-verified proof isn't automatically peer-reviewed. And OpenAI's so-called quasi-Riemann result does NOT mean AI solved the Riemann Hypothesis.

What's more interesting is how these discoveries were actually produced.

OpenAI reportedly used thousands of parallel AI agents to explore mathematical problems, including 10,000 concurrent instances targeting the Navier-Stokes equations. Human mathematicians selected problems, evaluated candidate proofs, prepared manuscripts, and used the Lean proof assistant to formally verify hundreds of results.

Some findings appear genuinely significant.

Barnette's Conjecture, open since 1969, now has a proposed complete Lean-verified proof. A non-sofic group construction challenges longstanding assumptions connected to Kaplansky's conjecture. Another result reportedly disproves Connes' Rigidity Conjecture, while an AI-generated unit-distance construction challenges a conjecture associated with Paul Erdős.

Then there's Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the rationals, potentially one of the biggest mathematical breakthroughs in decades. But the crucial limitation is that the claimed proof hasn't been made publicly available for independent examination.

And that's where the real controversy begins.

Mathematicians including Andreas Thom have challenged OpenAI's characterization of earlier research, raising questions about academic credit and the decades of human work underlying these discoveries. Meanwhile, researchers are still determining which results are genuinely new, which have been verified, and which require additional scrutiny.

OpenAI has formed an independent Math and AI Advisory Group involving prominent mathematicians including Timothy Gowers, Edward Witten, and Martin Hairer. But major questions remain about the unreleased model, its training data, the unsuccessful attempts, and whether AI-generated mathematics can be evaluated at the speed it's being produced.

We also compare OpenAI's approach with Google DeepMind, Anthropic's Claude, and existing formal theorem-proving systems like Lean and Coq.

The biggest story may not be that AI has solved mathematics. It may be that AI can now generate mathematical proof candidates faster than human experts can properly evaluate them.

So is this a historic breakthrough in automated mathematical discovery, an overhyped research announcement, or the beginning of an entirely different way of doing mathematics?

Watch the full breakdown to understand what OpenAI actually demonstrated, what remains unverified, and why the mathematical community is paying attention.

videos.summary_source_text:
Stop Setting Your Driver Up Wrong (Simple Address Fix) Master your driver set-up and discover exactly how to set the driver on the ground to master golf driver basics before you even begin your swing. Most golfers destroy their tee shots before the club even moves away from the ball.

In this video, we break down the critical fundamentals of setting the driver up to the golf ball. You'll learn: Grounding vs. Hovering: Why resting your driver flat behind the ball causes heel strikes, and why lining it up off the toe fixes centered contact. The Toe-Up Secret: Why your driver should sit 7° to 11° toe-up at address, and how forcing it flat destroys your posture, path, and swing speed. Driver Shaft Lean: The exact handle position relative to your lead thigh to prevent weak slices and delofting errors. The Lie Angle Shot-Shaping Hack: How altering your driver's lie angle at address unlocks an effortless draw or controlled fade without changing your swing mechanics.

videos.summary_source_text:
Sommarens enklaste fiskrecept smakar ännu godare i höstrusket Sej är den plånboksvänliga fisken som man lätt lagar gott med. 
Så här gjorde vi den i vedeldade ugnen och hjälp så gott det blir.
Blir ärligt talat precis lika god i vanliga ugnen hemma. Perfekt också till matlåda.

Videon är i samarbete med Seafood from Norway.
*Fler recept på norsk sej hittar du här:* https://bit.ly/4414Bsx

*Följ Louise Johansson på Instagram: https://bit.ly/3C5hV4q*

*Stekt sejrygg med tomat och pinjenötter*
En enkel och somrig rätt som du svänger ihop på 30 minuter. Servera gärna med nykokt färskpotatis och lite bröd som du kan dra upp det sista av såsen med. 

 4 portioner

600 g sejfilé
500 g vatten
50 g salt
400 g tomater, gärna olika sorter
1 kruka basilika
2 krm nymalen svartpeppar
1/2 dl olivolja
4 vitlöksklyftor, skivade
1/2 dl olivolja till servering
1 dl pinjenötter, rostade

Blanda vatten och 50 g salt till en rimlag. Lägg i fisken och rimma i 20 minuter. Ta upp och låt rinna av väl på hushållspapper så den blir torr. Ställ kallt i kylskåp tills den ska tillagas.

Skär tomaterna i bitar om 3 cm.
Grovhacka basilikan.

Smaksätt fisken med svartpeppar.

Stek fisken i 1/2 dl olja och vitlök på medelvärme ca 2-3 min på varje sida. Ös vitlöksoljan över fisken medan du steker. Lägg upp på ett fat.

Tillsätt tomaterna i stekpannan och stek ca 2-3 min. Smaksätt med salt och svartpeppar och vänd i basilikan.

Lägg tomaterna på fisken, ringla över resterande olivolja och strössla över pinjenötter.

Kör i ugnen på 150 grader tills fisken är precis klar. Sej är den plånboksvänliga fisken som man lätt lagar gott med.

Has Toyota forgotten how to build cars? New RAV4 Review Is this the new RAV4 must-have SUV of 2026?

Get 20% off CarVertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

This is the all-new Toyota RAV4! 

Mat’s got his hands on this all-new, family-friendly SUV to see if it has what it takes to compete with class leaders like the Volkswagen Tiguan and Jaecoo 8. The RAV4 rolls up with a hefty price rise since the previous iteration, but is it worth it? Let’s take a closer look, starting with the design… 

There’s no denying that the RAV4 looks pretty smart on the outside. We’ve got our hands on the mid-level iteration, and your attention is immediately drawn to the angular headlights and bonnet with creases that mimic the Land Cruiser. If you pick the GR version, you have a sportier front bumper than what we have here, but we think it looks more than good enough without upgrading. Along the side there are plastic surrounds on the wheel arches and along the sills, coupled with a load of creases along the length of the car. Around the back there are long taillights, a new RAV4 badge, and as with the front, GR editions come with a sportier bumper. All in all, it’s a good-looking car!

On the inside, there are several nods to the Land Cruiser, although you don’t have to look very far to find that many of the panels are covered in scratchy black plastic. Thankfully, though there are several saving graces, including a large infotainment screen that’s crisp and easy to use, and a whole load of storage throughout the cabin. There’s a digital dial screen which offers ok graphics, but the heads-up display is a nice touch. Ultimately it’s a fairly good cabin, but it doesn’t offer enough to notably stand out against the competition. 

All editions of the RAV4 are plug-in hybrids. The car we’re reviewing here comes with the entry-level powertrain - a 2.5-litre petrol engine, coupled with an electric motor, which drives the front wheels to deliver 272hp. It comes with a battery that allows for up to 75 miles driving on electric power alone, and it accelerates to 60mph in 7.5 seconds. The range-topper is a 2.5-litre PHEV that powers all four wheels, and this delivers 309hp. 

The RAV4 range starts from £44,195, rising all the way up to £52,045 for the GR Sport edition. But does it offer enough to lead you away from class leaders like the VW Tiguan? Let us know which you’d choose in the comments, then join Mat for this all-new in-depth review!

videos.title: DRAMATIC Ending in Madrid | 2026 Open de España
videos.summary_source_text:
DRAMATIC Ending in Madrid | 2026 Open de España Relive the Back Nine on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Grant Forrest secured victory in Madrid in dramatic fashion. videos.title: Burgerdudes Summer BBQ Burger [Recept]
videos.summary_source_text:
Burgerdudes Summer BBQ Burger [Recept] Hos oss är det sommar året om! Och du behöver faktiskt ingen grill för att göra en BBQ-burgare. Burgerdudes Summer BBQ Burger kombinerar Sweet Baby Ray's Original Barbecue Sauce med sallad, tomat och picklad rödlök. Den picklade rödlöken ger både krisp och syra som balanserar den söta och rökiga barbecuesåsen, medan grönsakerna lyfter smakerna. Vi smashar köttet på en stekplatta på grillen, men det går lika bra att göra det i en gjutjärnspanna i köket.

🍔 Burgerdudes Summer BBQ Burger
4 portioner / 30 min

Du behöver:
800 g grovmald högrevsfärs, 20–30 % fetthalt
4 hamburgerbröd, gärna briochebröd
8 skivor hamburgerost
Sweet Baby Ray's Original Barbecue Sauce
4 salladsblad
4 tomatskivor
1 rödlök
1 dl ättiksprit, 12 %
2 dl strösocker
3 dl vatten Smör
Salt och grovmald svartpeppar

Gör så här:
1.) Pickla rödlöken. Koka upp ättiksprit, socker och vatten och rör tills sockret har löst sig. Låt svalna. Skiva rödlöken tunt och lägg den i lagen i minst 30 minuter.
2.) Dela upp färsen i 8 delar à 100 gram och forma löst till bollar med händerna.
3.) Smält en liten klick smör på stekplattan eller i stekpannan och rosta insidan av bröden. Lägg åt sidan och torka av plattan eller pannan.
4.) Höj till maxvärme, cirka 250 grader. Lägg på köttbollarna och pressa med jämnt tryck till cirka 1 ½ cm tjocklek med ett smashverktyg i cirka 10 sekunder. Salta och peppra generöst.
5.) När små bubblor börjar bildas på köttets yta vänder du köttet med en vass stekspade. Lägg två skivor hamburgerost på varje köttpuck och stek ytterligare cirka 1 minut.
6.) Ringla Sweet Baby Ray's Original Barbecue Sauce på brödets botten och lock. Lägg ett salladsblad på botten, följt av två köttpuckar. Toppa med en tomatskiva och picklad rödlök. Sätt sedan på locket.

Servera direkt och njut av smaken av sommar! ☀️ Hos oss är det sommar året om! Och du behöver faktiskt ingen grill för att göra en BBQ-burgare. Monday With Meghan: Issues From Last Year Remain In Avalanche Loss to the Maple Leafs Toronto Maple Leafs overwhelm Colorado Avalanche with a 6-3 victory, raising critical questions around Colorado's goaltending. Can Mackenzie Blackwood seize the starter role, or will the Avalanche revisit last season’s persistent goalie concerns? Chris Micieli, Meghan Angley, and Zach Pearson break down Blackwood’s struggles, the team’s defensive lapses, and Coach Jared Bednar’s expectations as Avalanche fans speculate about the future between the pipes.

Special teams woes continue, with Colorado’s power play running cold after a hot start and the penalty kill showing uncharacteristic cracks. The hosts spotlight the need for a confidence boost and “greasy” goals, while offering an in-depth update on AHL prospects like Gavin Brindley and Taylor Makar with the Colorado Eagles. Can the Avalanche fix their lingering issues ahead of a back-to-back against the Dallas Stars, or are deeper changes on the horizon?

Never Consume These Foods Like This Stay safe and prioritize your health by avoiding these foods.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4AQP11s

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Because sometimes, a seemingly harmless ingredient can be harmful or even toxic.

Take potatoes, for instance. If they’re green, it means they contain high levels of solanine, which can cause digestive upset and other issues.

And then there’s bread and rice. Eating mold on these foods can cause harm to your liver and can even be carcinogenic.

Undercooked red kidney beans contain a chemical that causes your red blood cells and white blood cells to clump together, resulting in abdominal pain, vomiting, and more.

Undercooked hamburger meat can contain E. coli, particularly if it’s low-quality.

Then there’s the question of organic versus conventional foods.

Strawberries and chocolate, for example, are often heavily sprayed with pesticides, so avoid them unless they’re organic.

Even something as simple as raw almonds can pose an issue if they’re green and bitter, meaning they contain amygdalin, which can convert to cyanide in the body.

And let’s not forget about tap water. It contains various harmful contaminants, which is why a good filter is so important for your health.

It makes you wonder, doesn’t it? What other single factors might be quietly impacting your health in significant ways that you haven’t yet discovered?

Understanding your unique body and its specific needs can be a real game-changer.

videos.summary_source_text:
Eat This 1 Fruit Before Bed to Fall Asleep Faster and Sleep Longer!  Dr. Mandell What if one simple fruit before bedtime could make a difference in how you sleep, how your digestive system functions, and how you feel when you wake up? That fruit is kiwi! This small but powerful fruit contains natural serotonin, antioxidants, vitamin C, fiber, and a unique digestive enzyme called actinidin. Research suggests that eating kiwi before bed may help people fall asleep faster, improve sleep duration, and increase sleep efficiency. But the benefits don't stop there! Kiwi also supports healthy bowel movements, helps soften stool, and may relieve occasional constipation and digestive discomfort. Its natural fiber helps nourish beneficial gut bacteria, while actinidin assists with protein digestion. The connection between your gut and brain makes this fruit particularly interesting because both sleep and digestive health play important roles in your overall well-being. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the science behind kiwi, its potential benefits for sleep and colon health, and why adding one or two kiwis to your evening routine may be worth trying. Discover how something so simple could help you sleep more comfortably and support a healthier digestive system. Small daily habits can make a meaningful difference in your health!


PubMed Research

STATCAST: Maple Leafs vs Avs. One For the "Analytics Don't Matter" Crowd Colorado Avalanche dominate the analytics but fall 6-3 to the Toronto Maple Leafs—are the early cracks in defense cause for concern, or just an anomaly? Despite Nathan MacKinnon's electric two-goal night and an onslaught of scoring chances, the Avs’ special teams struggled with a 0-for-5 power play and defensive lapses that allowed stars like William Nylander and Auston Matthews too much room to operate.

Statcast breaks down the disconnect between Colorado’s eye-popping stats—outshooting the Leafs 33-23, dominating Corsi, and generating waves of high-danger chances—and the disappointing result on the scoreboard. Key discussion points include Nick Roy’s defensive miscues, Mackenzie Blackwood’s rough outing in net, and whether these familiar issues signal a trend or just a bump in the young season. Can the Avs’ top line maintain their offensive firepower while tightening up at the back?

videos.title: GPT-6 Astra Is Now COMPLETELY FREE with Intelligent UI!
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6 Astra Is Now COMPLETELY FREE with Intelligent UI! https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI just released GPT-6 for everyone, including free ChatGPT users. And its flagship model, GPT-6 Astra, reportedly scored an astonishing 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3, a reasoning benchmark where previous-generation AI models struggled to reach double digits.

But here's the twist: the GPT-6 model achieving those extraordinary benchmark results isn't the one most people will use. And OpenAI's most interesting new feature, Intelligent UI, doesn't even work with its most powerful model.

On October 7, 2026, OpenAI announced "GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone," introducing three AI models and a completely different way to interact with ChatGPT.

Instead of simply generating text, ChatGPT can now create interactive calculators, clickable diagrams, live charts, forms, simulations, and even playable mini-games directly inside conversations.

But does Intelligent UI actually work beyond OpenAI's carefully selected demos?

And how much better is GPT-6 compared to GPT-5.6, Claude, and Gemini?

First, there's the new GPT-6 model lineup.

GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's flagship reasoning model, featuring a context window exceeding one million tokens and a reported 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 score.

GPT-6 Sol is the everyday workhorse for paid subscribers. According to OpenAI, it produces roughly 50% fewer factual errors than GPT-5.6 Sol, improves AutomationBench performance from 20.3% to 33.2%, and delivers faster responses.

But the bigger story might be Intelligent UI.

OpenAI has introduced a system that lets ChatGPT generate functional interfaces on demand. Ask for a retirement calculator, and instead of explaining compound interest, ChatGPT creates input fields and an interactive growth chart. Ask about probability, and it can build a simulation. Need to split a restaurant bill? It can generate a calculator directly inside your conversation.

Under the hood, Intelligent UI uses native, streamable interface components rather than executing arbitrary HTML or JavaScript on your device.

OpenAI demonstrated interactive bicycle diagrams, central limit theorem simulations, retirement calculators, and even a retro arcade shooter.

But demonstrations aren't the same as real-world testing.

So I tested GPT-6 Intelligent UI myself using three practical challenges.

First, I asked ChatGPT to create an interactive solar system where I could adjust a planet's orbital distance. It generated a visual representation, but the requested orbital adjustment wasn't fully functional.

Next, I tested a retirement savings calculator using age, monthly contributions, retirement age, and interest rate. This worked much closer to expectations, generating interactive inputs and updating the projected savings chart when values changed.

The results revealed an important limitation: Intelligent UI can create useful interfaces, but its input validation and reliability aren't always comparable to traditional software.

And there's another major catch.

GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's most powerful model, doesn't support Intelligent UI in its Pro compute mode. The interactive features run on GPT-6 Sol and Luna instead.

We also examine OpenAI's reported benchmark improvements.

GPT-6 Sol scores 68.8% on DeepSWE compared with GPT-5.6's 65.2%, while Claude Fable 5.1 reportedly scores 69.9%.

On FrontierCode 1.1, Sol reaches 49.3% versus Claude Fable 5.1's 50.9%, with OpenAI reporting approximately 37% lower inference cost per task.

OpenAI also claims GPT-6 begins streaming responses 44% sooner.

However, these benchmark results come from OpenAI's own published evaluations and haven't all been independently verified.

There are significant restrictions: no public Intelligent UI API, limited support in older desktop apps, and no interactive interface when using Astra's highest compute tier.

The larger question is whether OpenAI is moving beyond traditional chatbots toward AI-generated software.

That's an ambitious direction, but the current implementation still has limitations.

So is GPT-6 genuinely a major breakthrough? Is Intelligent UI the beginning of a new software paradigm, or just an impressive feature that still needs serious refinement?

Watch the full breakdown for hands-on GPT-6 testing, Intelligent UI demonstrations, benchmark comparisons, important limitations, and what OpenAI's latest release actually means for everyday users.

Subscribe to BitBiased for independent AI testing, OpenAI updates, model comparisons, cybersecurity, and emerging technology coverage.

02:00 What OpenAI Actually Shipped

06:52 What Happened When I Actually Tested It
10:01 Whether the Numbers Actually Hold Up

14:24 The Verdict

👉 Start your meal with veggies - a green salad, roasted asparagus, anything that has plenty of fiber. Fiber forms a protective mesh in your gut, which slows down digestion and helps glucose enter your bloodstream more gradually.

👉 Move your muscles after you eat - walking for 10 minutes, dancing, doing a few squats… pick your favourite. Your muscles use glucose for fuel, helping reduce the spike.

👉 Try apple cider vinegar before a carb-heavy meal - 1 tbsp diluted in a large glass of water. The acetic acid in vinegar can slow the rate at which glucose enters your bloodstream.

1 cup (210 g) beans. Soak in water for 6 hrs.
Cook until the beans are tender.
1/4 cup (30 g) sesame seeds.
3 cups (750 ml) bean cooking water.
1/2 cup (125 ml) coconut cream.
Heat well, but do not boil.
Store in the fridge for up to 3 days.

videos.summary_source_text:
5 Surprising Reasons You Fart and How to Stop Did you know the average person farts between 5 and 15 times a day?

Flatulence is a normal bodily function.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/47cjk5i

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

But if you’re experiencing it frequently, or if it’s accompanied by discomfort, it might be time to address the underlying cause.

One common factor is low stomach acidity.

When you have low stomach acid, food can pass through your body undigested.

This can create excess gas, bloating, and discomfort.

Supporting healthy stomach acid levels with apple cider vinegar can make a difference.

Food intolerances are another common cause.

Many people lack the enzymes needed to properly break down certain foods, like dairy or gluten.

Consuming probiotic-rich foods can support your body’s ability to produce enzymes and aid digestion.

Then there are gas-producing foods like fruit, beans, starches, and sugars.

It’s best to avoid these if you’re concerned with flatulence.

Even habits like chewing gum or drinking carbonated beverages can contribute to excess gas by causing you to swallow more air.

It really makes you wonder: What else might be impacting your body in ways you don’t realize?

Often, the biggest obstacle when trying to improve your health isn’t a lack of effort, but a misunderstanding of what’s truly going on beneath the surface.

If you’ve been searching for the one thing that could kickstart your journey to better health, but struggling to find it… you’re not broken.

You may just be focusing on the wrong thing.

videos.title: Inconsistent ball striking? Change your HANDS!!
videos.summary_source_text:
Inconsistent ball striking? Change your HANDS!! If you’re struggling with inconsistent ball striking, chunks, thin shots, or a golf swing that feels all arms, look down before you start changing what your hands are doing. 👀⛳️

Train your pressure shift with the Ball First Board: https://improve.shotcraftgolf.com/products/bfb/lp2?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=social&utm_content=youtube-short-Sliding-hips-feet-pressure2

Your pressure shift might be the missing piece.
Watch the feet and hips closely in this video, because the important part isn’t just where your weight goes, it’s when it gets there.

In the backswing, pressure loads into the trail side, staying more toward the inside of the trail foot rather than drifting to the outside.

But here’s the part a lot of golfers miss:
You don’t wait until the backswing is finished to start moving toward the target.
As the club is finishing the backswing, pressure is already beginning to move toward the lead side.

That gives you a better opportunity to rotate through the shot instead of:
→ Hanging back on your trail foot
→ Sliding through impact
→ Throwing the arms at the ball
→ Trying to save the strike at the last second

Think of the sequence as:
LOAD → SHIFT → ROTATE

Not:
LOAD → WAIT → PANIC. 😅

And this is why simply watching weight-shift videos can only get you so far.
You may understand exactly what you’re supposed to do and still have no idea whether you’re actually doing it.

That’s the problem the Ball First Board is designed to solve.

It gives you physical feedback for the trail-side load, helps prevent excessive sway, and gives you a reference for moving into the lead side so you can train the movement you’re seeing in this video instead of guessing.

If you’re tired of knowing what a good golf swing should look like but struggling to reproduce the feeling, this is where I’d start.

Watch the video again and pay attention only to the feet this time. Then save it for your next range session.

videos.title: Worried About Clogged Arteries? Drink This!  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Worried About Clogged Arteries? Drink This!  Dr. Mandell Discover how five simple ingredients may help promote healthy blood flow, nitric oxide production, and better circulation! In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell shares an easy-to-make morning shot combining beetroot, turmeric, ginger, fresh lemon juice, and cayenne pepper. Beetroot provides natural dietary nitrates that the body can convert into nitric oxide, helping blood vessels relax and supporting healthy blood pressure. Turmeric contains curcumin, a compound studied for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, while ginger contains beneficial plant compounds being investigated for cardiovascular health. Lemon provides vitamin C, and cayenne contains capsaicin, which has also attracted interest for its potential vascular and metabolic effects. Together, these ingredients offer a simple way to incorporate beneficial plant compounds into your daily routine. Remember, maintaining healthy arteries requires more than one drink. Regular exercise, nutritious whole foods, adequate sleep, healthy blood pressure, and stress management are essential for long-term cardiovascular wellness.

INGREDIENTS:

¼ teaspoon beetroot powder OR 1 teaspoon beetroot juice
¼ teaspoon turmeric powder
¼ teaspoon ginger powder
1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice
A small pinch of cayenne pepper
Water as needed to mix

HOW TO PREPARE:

Combine the beetroot powder or juice, turmeric, ginger, fresh lemon juice, and cayenne pepper in a small bowl or shot glass. Add a little water to reach your preferred consistency, stir thoroughly, and drink freshly prepared. You may enjoy this shot in the morning or at another convenient time. Taking it on an empty stomach is not necessary, especially if you are sensitive to acidic or spicy foods. The nitrate content of beetroot products varies, and the small amount used in this recipe has not been established as an effective dose for lowering blood pressure.

SELECTED SCIENTIFIC REFERENCES (PubMed):

Lundberg JO, Weitzberg E, Gladwin MT. The nitrate–nitrite–nitric oxide pathway in physiology and therapeutics. Nature Reviews Drug Discovery. 2008;7:156–167. PMID: 18167491.

Kapil V, Haydar SM, Pearl V, et al. Physiological role for nitrate-reducing oral bacteria in blood-pressure control. Free Radical Biology and Medicine. 2013. PMID: 23624383.

Nicoll R, Henein MY. Ginger and cardiovascular disease: A systematic review. International Journal of Cardiology. 2009. PMID: 18178243.

These references provide background on individual ingredients and biological mechanisms, not clinical proof of the complete five-ingredient recipe.

videos.title: xAI's Grok 5: Elon Musk's 1 MILLION GPU Ambition!
videos.summary_source_text:
xAI's Grok 5: Elon Musk's 1 MILLION GPU Ambition! https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Elon Musk said Grok 5 would launch in Q1 2026 with 6 trillion parameters and a 10% chance of achieving AGI. But it's now October, Grok 5 still hasn't launched, and xAI has never officially confirmed those numbers.

Meanwhile, Grok 4.7 just delivered an enormous benchmark jump: Terminal-Bench performance surged from 20.3% to 37.6%, an improvement of roughly 85% over Grok 4.6. And that might be our clearest indication yet of what xAI is building toward with Grok 5.

But there's a catch hiding inside those benchmark results.

xAI has released three major model updates in roughly ten weeks: Grok 4.5 in July, Grok 4.6 in August, and Grok 4.7 on September 21. The latest release introduces a new, larger base model, extended reinforcement learning, and training focused on complex tasks that can take hours to complete.

That's a significant shift from simply improving an existing model. And it raises an important question: Is Grok 4.7 an early preview of the technology behind Grok 5?

We examine what xAI has actually confirmed about Grok 5, what Elon Musk has claimed, and why the distinction matters. The rumored 6-trillion-parameter architecture, Q1 release window, and AGI predictions remain unverified. The only official confirmation is that Grok 5 was in training.

Then we break down Grok 4.7's performance across coding, engineering, medical reasoning, and autonomous agent benchmarks.

According to xAI's published results:

- Terminal-Bench: 20.3% → 37.6%
- CursorBench: 40.4% → 46.3%
- DeepSWE: 65.2% → 71.0%
- EEBench: 53.0% → 64.0%
- HealthBench Pro: 48.5% → 56.7%

Those gains look impressive, especially for long-running coding agents. But the tests were conducted by xAI using high reasoning effort, with limited public details about the evaluation methodology and no independent reproduction of the reported results.

And despite the improvements, Grok 4.7 still trails competitors in several important areas.

Claude Fable 5.1 reportedly scores 57.9% on Terminal-Bench versus Grok's 37.6%. GPT-5.6 Sol remains ahead on medical reasoning, while Grok takes a notable lead in engineering reasoning with its 64.0% EEBench score.

The competitive picture is much more complicated than a single benchmark chart suggests.

Pricing adds another dimension. Grok 4.7 costs $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, compared with $4 and $20 for GPT-5.6 Sol on xAI's comparison chart.

With a 500,000-token context window, image input, function calling, web search, X search, code execution, and integration into Cursor and Grok Build, xAI is positioning Grok as a serious option for developers building AI agents.

But can those agents actually complete complicated work reliably?

We investigate xAI's claims about Grok Bot, including a reported internal workflow involving hundreds of agentic steps and a five-person team merging more than 100 pull requests daily. We also explain why impressive internal demonstrations aren't the same as independently verified real-world reliability.

Then there's the infrastructure behind everything.

xAI has officially reported access to more than one million H100 GPU equivalents. Its massive Colossus computing infrastructure provides important context for the company's rapid release cycle, although the specific hardware training Grok 5 remains unconfirmed.

Ultimately, Grok 5 faces a much harder challenge than delivering another impressive announcement.

It needs to close the gap with Claude and GPT-5.6 on demanding agentic benchmarks, improve reliability on long-running tasks, and potentially move beyond the text-only output limitations of Grok 4.7.

So is xAI approaching a genuine breakthrough, or is the gap between Musk's promises and the actual product getting harder to ignore?

Watch the full breakdown to understand what Grok 4.7 reveals, what the benchmarks leave unanswered, and what Grok 5 would actually need to deliver.

videos.title: GPT-6.1 Sol: 10 Prompts That Will Save Your Lot of Time
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6.1 Sol: 10 Prompts That Will Save Your Lot of Time https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

GPT-6.1 Sol is supposed to make roughly 32% fewer factual mistakes than GPT-6 Sol on hard questions, while costing about one-fifth as much per token as GPT-6 Astra. But benchmark numbers don’t tell you what happens when you actually sit down and use it.

So this video skips the benchmark charts and tests GPT-6.1 Sol with the kinds of prompts normal people actually type: learning a difficult topic, rewriting an email, researching current products, analyzing PDFs and spreadsheets, building and debugging code, and making everyday decisions.

According to OpenAI’s own figures, Sol’s error rate on hard factual questions drops from 11.4% with GPT-6 Sol to 7.7%. It costs $2 per million input tokens compared with Astra’s $10, while OpenAI says it gets surprisingly close to Astra on coding and document work.

Sol also has a context window of roughly 1.05 million tokens, making long documents and complex projects one of its most interesting use cases. Its knowledge cutoff is April 30, 2026, however, so anything newer still requires web search.

But the bigger lesson here isn’t about specifications. It’s about how little prompting you actually need.

For learning, we start with a difficult topic and simply ask Sol to explain it in plain language using one everyday analogy. Then we increase the difficulty without restarting the conversation. The same approach turns Sol into a basic tutor for Python: explain the concept, give me an exercise, and don’t reveal the solution until I ask.

For writing, we test whether Sol can take an ordinary email and make it professional without making it sound robotic. Tiny follow-ups like “make it shorter” and “make it less formal” quickly produce completely different versions without requiring elaborate prompts.

Research is where things get more serious. Sol compares current AI video generators using web search, but instead of simply trusting the answer, we ask it to show the sources behind its main claims and identify the information it’s least confident about. That extra step matters when prices, features, and product details can change quickly.

Then we move into files.

A real PDF gets turned into 10 bullet points and then condensed again into five key takeaways. A spreadsheet gets analyzed using normal questions like “Which category has the highest total spending?” before Sol calculates totals and averages by category.

For coding, we go from one sentence — “Create a simple expense calculator in HTML” — to a working tool. Then we add dark mode and CSV downloads with another short instruction. We also give Sol broken Python code and ask it to find the problem, fix it, and explain the mistake simply.

Finally, there’s one prompting technique that works almost everywhere: make Sol interview you first.

Instead of dumping every detail into a giant prompt, ask it to question you about your needs before recommending something. We test that approach with choosing between a laptop and desktop, creating a meal plan, and planning a weekend getaway.

Sol still needs supervision. OpenAI’s own testing shows it can make factual mistakes, current information requires web search, and code, calculations, and important claims should still be checked.

But you don’t need complicated “prompt engineering” to get substantially better answers. Seven tiny follow-ups handle most of the work: make it shorter, explain it simply, give me an example, put this in a table, check your answer, show me your sources, and ask me questions first.

A student texted Eric Cogorno after leaving his golf school to say he shot the best round of his life — and all he changed was three trail shoulder moves in the golf downswing sequence. Most golfers trying to stop coming over the top are focused on their arms or their hips, but the real fix is simpler: get the trail shoulder down, keep it down, and get it forward. Eric breaks down exactly how golf side bend and hip rotation work together to lower the trail shoulder, move the golf low point control forward, and keep the body a consistent distance from the ground through the follow through. The club across shoulders drill gives any golfer an instant visual checkpoint — close your left eye and you can see the club head get right behind the golf ball when the trail shoulder is in the correct golf impact position. If you leave this video without trying the club across shoulders drill, you're leaving golf low point control and consistent iron contact on the table.

What You'll Learn:
• Why getting the trail shoulder down in the golf downswing sequence creates an inside club path and prevents pulls and fades
• How golf side bend — right shoulder getting closer to the right hip — combines with hip rotation to lower the trail shoulder
• Why the forward component of the trail shoulder move is what shifts golf low point control past the ball for ball first contact
• Why keeping the trail shoulder down in the follow through maintains a consistent body distance from the ground
• The club across shoulders drill: how to see and feel the correct trail shoulder depth and forward position at golf impact position
• The right side oblique crunch feel for training correct golf side bend through the ball
• How combining the oblique crunch with chest out towards the target delivers the complete down and forward trail shoulder motion
• How to hit irons more solid by training all three moves — down, keep down, forward — in sequence

videos.title: Once You Understand This, The Golf Swing Becomes Effortless
videos.summary_source_text:
Once You Understand This, The Golf Swing Becomes Effortless Want a golf swing that feels smoother, more natural and more powerful without feeling like you have to swing harder?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn a simple golf swing concept that can help you create more effortless speed by using the golf club as a lever rather than lifting it into position.

This is especially useful if your golf swing feels forced, you struggle to create clubhead speed, or you feel like you have to work too hard to hit the golf ball further.

Danny Maude uses a simple sledgehammer analogy to explain how the golf club should move in the backswing, why many golfers lose leverage, and how to let the weight of the club create a more natural and powerful downswing.

Practice Plan
I've put this weeks video into a practice plan you can take to the range and follow step by step. Hope it helps: https://www.dannymaude.com/learn-this-for-an-effortless-golf-swing

In this golf lesson, you’ll learn:

• How to make the golf swing feel more effortless  
• How to create clubhead speed without swinging harder  
• Why lifting the golf club can rob you of power  
• How to use the golf club as a lever  
• Why the butt of the grip should feel like it moves down  
• How to create better leverage in the backswing  
• How the body naturally responds to the weight of the club  
• Why forcing positions can make the golf swing harder  
• How to let momentum create more speed through impact  
• Why using the hands correctly can improve power  
• A simple golf drill using two clubs to feel the lever  
• How to use your camera to check your golf swing  

If your golf swing feels tense, disconnected or underpowered, this drill can help you experience a completely different way of moving the club.

The goal is not to manufacture more positions. It is to understand how leverage, weight and momentum can work together so the golf club starts to feel easier to move and speed becomes a by-product of a better motion.

Walking is one of the simplest ways to support your overall health, but a few small changes can make it even more effective. 

Walking benefits include:
• Supports cardiovascular health
• Supports metabolic health
• Supports brain health and cognitive function
• Promotes better mental health
• Improves sleep quality
• Supports a healthy body composition
• Strengthens muscles and joints
• Helps reduce stress
• Supports immune function
• Supports eye health

Some people focus so much on their step count that they overlook the quality of those steps. Varying your walking pace and terrain can help you get more out of your walking exercise.

Walking outside can boost the benefits even further by adding sun exposure. If possible, walk with a friend or family member to add the benefits of social connection.

It’s time for an incredible Porsche head-to-head! 

We’ve got our hands on the all-new Porsche Cayenne Turbo, and it’s lining up against the all-new Porsche 911 Turbo S! 

We all know by now that the 911 Turbo S rolls up with hybrid power, but the all-new Cayenne is 100% electric! But does this huge SUV have what it takes to bring down this incredible sports car? Let’s take a closer look at the stats… 

Starting with the 911 Turbo S, it’s powered by a 3.6-litre twin-turbo flat-six hybrid, and it puts down 711hp and 800Nm. This power is sent to all four wheels, and it weighs in at 1,740kg.

Then we come to the Cayenne Turbo. It’s powered by two electric motors, and these combine to produce an incredible 1,156hp and 1,500Nm! It may be heavy, tipping the scales at 2,645kg, but it still launches like a rocket ship! 

So will the instant acceleration of the electric Cayenne propel it to victory? Or will the significantly lighter 911 snatch the win? There’s only one way to find out for sure… LET’S RACE!

videos.title: 09.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
09.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
PREVIEW: Avalanche Get Their First Look at Gavin McKenna and the Toronto Maple Leafs The Toronto Maple Leafs face a pivotal test against the high-flying Colorado Avalanche. Can Auston Matthews and William Nylander break Toronto’s streak of inconsistency, or will Colorado’s explosive offense and home-ice advantage be too much to overcome?

The conversation focused on key stat matchups, defensive upgrades for the Maple Leafs including the addition of Darren Raddysh and Sergei Bobrovsky’s goaltending struggles, and standout rookie performances from Gavin McKenna and Easton Cowan. Several points were raised, including Toronto’s strong penalty kill, issues with defensive cohesion, and Colorado’s dominance in shot speed, scoring chances, and offensive zone time. The discussion explored whether Toronto’s revamped lineup can slow down the Avalanche, and what this game could mean for both teams’ playoff outlooks. Will the Maple Leafs seize the moment or continue to tread water in the standings?

videos.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 Is Here: 10X Cheaper Than GPT-6 Luna?
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Haiku 5.5 Is Here: 10X Cheaper Than GPT-6 Luna? https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Anthropic just released Claude Haiku 5.5, and the numbers are hard to ignore: a 90% price cut, a massive 1-million-token context window, and a jump from 15.7% to 72.4% on OSWorld, a benchmark that tests whether AI can actually operate a computer.

But here's the real question: can Anthropic's cheapest AI model outperform OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna while costing exactly the same?

Released October 7, 2026, Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's latest small AI model, designed for speed, affordability, coding, automation, and high-volume enterprise workloads. With API pricing starting at just $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, Anthropic is making a serious play for the budget AI market.

And this isn't just about cheaper AI.

Haiku 5.5 introduces adaptive thinking with adjustable reasoning effort, image understanding, browser capabilities, and a context window five times larger than its predecessor. It's available through the Claude API, Claude apps, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.

The benchmark improvements are particularly interesting.

On OSWorld, Haiku 5.5 scores 72.4%, compared to just 15.7% for the previous Haiku. On Terminal-Bench, its agentic coding performance jumps from 0% to 39.2%. And on Humanity's Last Exam, it reaches 45.9% without tools and 57.4% with tools.

Against OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna, Haiku 5.5 reportedly leads on several shared benchmarks, including agentic coding (39.2% versus 16.4%) and visual reasoning (46.4% versus 29.1%).

But benchmark scores don't always translate into real-world performance.

That's why I put Claude Haiku 5.5 through practical tests against GPT-6 Luna, including building a playable Python Snake game with Pygame, debugging JavaScript, solving a multi-layered logic puzzle, and extracting messy information into structured JSON.

These tests focus on the tasks developers and businesses actually care about: coding accuracy, reasoning, speed, cost, and reliable automation.

Then there's the pricing catch.

Anthropic advertises a 90% reduction compared to the previous Haiku generation, but the cheapest rates only apply to prompts below 100,000 tokens. Cross that threshold, and pricing increases fivefold to $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens.

That makes the million-token context window impressive, but potentially much more expensive than the headline pricing suggests.

We also compare Haiku 5.5 against Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5, OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6 Sol, and Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite.

Can Haiku really handle serious agentic coding? Is its long-context reasoning reliable? Does adaptive thinking make a meaningful difference? And can a model this cheap replace more expensive AI systems for everyday business automation?

There are important limitations, too. Sonnet and Opus still outperform Haiku on difficult reasoning and complex coding tasks. Long-context instruction retention isn't perfect, hallucinations remain a concern, and a 39.2% Terminal-Bench score still leaves significant room for improvement.

The bigger story is what this release means for the AI industry.

If affordable models can handle classification, customer support, summarization, data processing, and routine coding, businesses may no longer need expensive flagship models for every task.

Anthropic is betting on a future where Haiku handles the volume, Sonnet handles more demanding work, and Opus tackles the hardest problems.

And with OpenAI and Google competing for the same market, the battle for affordable AI is getting much more interesting.

Watch the full breakdown to see where Claude Haiku 5.5 delivers, where the benchmarks need context, and whether its price-to-performance ratio makes it worth switching.

videos.title: Gemini Spark Explained: Google’s AI That Works While You Sleep
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini Spark Explained: Google’s AI That Works While You Sleep Typeless turns messy thoughts into clear and polished writing, and is now available on Linux. It helps developers to speak to AI agents with detailed prompts and context effortlessly, across browsers, terminals, IDEs, and other apps.Try Typeless: https://www.typeless.com/?via=1003

Google's Gemini Spark can keep working even after you close your laptop. It can manage Gmail, edit Google Docs, control Chrome, organize files, and execute multi-step tasks while you sleep. But independent testing reveals some surprising failures — including an AI agent that reportedly couldn't save a simple packing list to Google Keep.

So is Google Spark really a 24/7 AI employee, or just another AI assistant with a much bigger permission slip?

Announced at Google I/O in May 2026, Gemini Spark is Google's persistent AI agent, powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash and an internal orchestration system called Antigravity. Unlike regular Gemini chat or Gemini Deep Research, Spark operates on dedicated cloud virtual machines, allowing tasks to continue without your device staying online.

And Google's rollout has been aggressive. In roughly ten weeks, Spark went from an AI Ultra-only U.S. beta to a globally available agent for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers across more than 160 countries.

But the real story isn't how quickly Google launched Spark. It's what happens when you give an AI agent access to your digital life.

Spark can search Gmail, draft emails, update Google Sheets, create presentations, manage Calendar events, and interact with websites through Chrome. It also connects to outside services including Canva, OpenTable, Instacart, Dropbox, and Zillow using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

On Mac, Connected Folders even allow Spark to edit and reorganize local files within explicitly authorized directories.

That sounds like a serious step toward autonomous AI. Until you examine the restrictions.

Google has built an approval system into Spark. Reading connected data generally requires no additional confirmation, but sending messages, making purchases, submitting external forms, and other consequential actions require human approval.

Then there are the reliability problems.

In independent testing reported by AI Chat Daily, Spark handled several everyday errands successfully but stumbled over basic instructions. It reportedly substituted a Google Doc when asked to save a packing list in Keep, returned four newsletter articles instead of five, and configured a price-monitoring task with a schedule that could miss short-lived discounts.

These aren't necessarily catastrophic failures. But they're important when the entire selling point is letting an AI work without constant supervision.

And access isn't free.

Google AI Pro costs $19.99 per month, while AI Ultra costs $99.99 per month. Spark also consumes your existing Gemini usage allowance rather than providing a separate unlimited pool. Regional restrictions further complicate availability, particularly across the EU, UK, Switzerland, and Nigeria.

Privacy raises another question. To function effectively, Spark may need access to emails, documents, calendar entries, browser sessions, and connected third-party accounts. Google says private content isn't used for model training without the relevant permissions, but automated browsing can still expose information to external websites.

Then there's Google's performance marketing.

Google highlighted a claim that Gemini 3.5 Flash generates tokens roughly 4x faster than GPT-4. But GPT-4 launched back in 2023. Comparing Spark's underlying model against an older OpenAI system doesn't establish how it performs against newer agent-focused competitors.

With OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's frontier models competing in the AI agent space, the more meaningful question isn't raw token speed. It's whether these systems can reliably finish real tasks.

This breakdown examines what Gemini Spark actually does, how its permissions work, where independent testing found limitations, what subscribers pay, and whether Google's vision of an always-working AI assistant is ready for everyday use.

Because there's a major difference between an AI that can take action and an AI you can trust to take action without watching it.

videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Spela golf hemma året runt… Efter många frågor tar jag med er till tre olika simulatorlösningar för att ge er inspiration till vintern och många roliga timmar. www.easygreen.se www.golfstudiosweden.se

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

videos.title: 08.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
08.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 08.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text: Just like Tiger Woods in 2000 Click the link in bio for the lowest price on the ball first board! Breaking down the biggest consistency killer I see in most golf swings: syncing your weight shift with your backswing and downswing so it feels all arms. Using my Ball First board, I show how the weight shift should precede the arms, just like Tiger Woods in 2000. I demonstrate how to start with a small pressure bump into the trail side before the backswing (without swaying into the right stick), then squat and bump down-and-left to load the lead leg before the downswing. The key sequence is “bump, turn, bump, turn,” so the lower body shifts first and the arms follow through. I also explain how you can practice this at home, on the range, or on the course, and where to find the link to the board while supplies last. videos.summary_source_text:
Linn Grant’s Unusual Golf Swing Left Us Seriously Impressed ⛳️ Take Your FREE Game Assessment → https://meandmygolf.com/game-plan/?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Description&utm_campaign=08.10.26

📱 Download the Swing Coach App (2-Week Free Trial) → https://go.meandmygolf.com/swingcoach/yt/?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Description&utm_campaign=08.10.26

Linn Grant has one of the most unusual golf swings in professional golf. Her shaft becomes remarkably vertical in the backswing, but the way she shallows the club and delivers it with the driver left us seriously impressed.
